prompt: Explain how vaccines train the immune system.
text:
Vaccines train the immune system by mimicking an infectious agent. They introduce a harmless part of the virus or bacterium, such as a protein or a piece of its genetic material, into the body. This part is known as an antigen. When the immune system detects the antigen, it recognizes it as foreign and mounts an immune response.
